title: "Calculations"

The graphene structure builder is in `01_graphene/`. The first local MACE
relaxations of two-vacancy 4 × 4 and 5 × 5 cells are complete in
`02_vacancy_relaxation/`. The larger 20 × 20 and 21 × 21 set is in
`03_vacancy_relaxation_20_21/`. The two-vacancy formation-energy scan from
2 × 2 through 10 × 10 is complete in `04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/`.

## Local calculation 01: graphene

[`make_graphene.py`](01_graphene/make_graphene.py) uses ASE to build an
$n \times n$ graphene supercell containing $2n^2$ carbon atoms. It defaults to
$a = 2.46$ Å and 15 Å vacuum on each side, with periodicity in-plane only.
These are starting geometry settings, not converged calculation parameters.

From the paper directory, using the existing local ASE environment:

```sh
../../AgI/agi-hexatic/.venv/bin/python calculations/01_graphene/make_graphene.py 4
```

The output is `calculations/01_graphene/graphene_4x4.extxyz`; a 32-carbon example
has been generated locally. Structure checks for $n=1,3,4$ confirmed atom counts,
cell geometry, vacuum, periodicity, three neighbours per carbon and bond lengths.
Use `--a`, `--vacuum` and `--output` to change the settings or destination.
See the [calculation README](01_graphene/README.md) for environment setup.

## Local calculation 02: two-vacancy relaxation

Both honeycomb vacancy patterns were relaxed with the locally available
[MACE-MPA-0 medium foundation model](https://mace-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide/foundation_models.html),
using `/opt/anaconda3/envs/mace/bin/python`, MACE 0.3.16, CPU and float64.
The checkpoint checksum and package versions are recorded with the calculation.

The periodic cells stay fixed at $a=2.46$ Å, with 15 Å vacuum on each side;
all atomic coordinates relax in 3D. A small reproducible perturbation allows
symmetry breaking. ASE BFGS stopped when the largest force was below 0.005 eV/Å.

| Cell | Carbon atoms | Steps | Final max force (eV/Å) | Max $|\mathbf{u}_{\parallel}|$ (Å) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 × 4 | 30 | 22 | 0.003587 | 0.055897 |
| 5 × 5 | 48 | 18 | 0.004394 | 0.082216 |

Displacements are relative to the ideal surviving sites, with periodic wrapping
and rigid translation removed. The primary quantity is
$|\mathbf{u}_{\parallel}|=\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}$; the strain tensor has not been computed.
These are exploratory foundation-model results with fixed cells.

See the [method and reproduction commands](02_vacancy_relaxation/README.md),
[relaxation script](02_vacancy_relaxation/relax.py), and
[Figure 1](../fig1_strain/notes.qmd) for plots. Atom-resolved data are in the
[4 × 4 CSV](02_vacancy_relaxation/4x4/displacement.csv) and
[5 × 5 CSV](02_vacancy_relaxation/5x5/displacement.csv).

## Local calculation 03: 20 × 20 and 21 × 21

The [larger-cell set](03_vacancy_relaxation_20_21/README.md) uses the same pinned
MACE-MPA-0 medium model, fixed lattice constant, vacuum, 3D atomic relaxation,
starting perturbation and force tolerance as calculation 02.

| Cell | Carbon atoms | Original vacancy indices | Parent sublattices | Vacancy spacing (Å) |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| 20 × 20 | 798 | 0, 267 | A, B | 28.405633 |
| 21 × 21 | 880 | 0, 322 | A, A | 29.825915 |

Both use full-cell fractional vacancy positions $(0,0)$ and $(1/3,2/3)$.
Explicit 7 × 7 repeats verified equal nearest distances and 120° angles at
all 50 interior vacancy sites for each case. The exact 21 × 21 honeycomb pattern
requires same-sublattice vacancies, so this comparison changes the parent
sublattice arrangement as well as cell size.

Both cells converged and passed fresh force evaluations of their saved structures.

| Cell | BFGS steps | Final max force (eV/Å) | Max $|\mathbf{u}_{\parallel}|$ (Å) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 20 × 20 | 89 | 0.004324 | 0.334622 |
| 21 × 21 | 29 | 0.004811 | 0.106652 |

The 20 × 20 result has a reconstructed neighbour pair of about 1.813 Å at each
vacancy; the 21 × 21 result retains approximately threefold neighbour-pair
distances of 2.28–2.30 Å at the selected force tolerance. These are different local
vacancy geometries as well as different parent sublattice arrangements.

See [Figure 1](../fig1_strain/notes.qmd) for the vector and Gouraud views. The
atom-resolved data are in the
[20 × 20 CSV](03_vacancy_relaxation_20_21/20x20/displacement.csv) and
[21 × 21 CSV](03_vacancy_relaxation_20_21/21x21/displacement.csv).

## Local calculation 04: formation energies, 2 × 2 through 10 × 10

The [04 set](04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/README.md) uses the same model and
fixed-cell relaxation protocol. Its carbon reference is the perfect two-atom
graphene primitive cell at the matching lattice constant $a=2.46$ Å:

$$
\mu_\mathrm{C}=\frac{E_\mathrm{perfect\ unit}}{2}=-9.2038120651\;\mathrm{eV/C},
\qquad
E_\mathrm{form}=E_\mathrm{relaxed\ defect}-(2n^2-2)\mu_\mathrm{C}.
$$

$n$ denotes the supercell repeat size, while $N_\mathrm{C}=2n^2-2$ is the
surviving atom count. The formation energy is for **two vacancies per cell**;
the average per vacancy is half this value.

| Cell | Carbon atoms | Parent sublattices | $E_\mathrm{form}$, two vacancies (eV) | Per vacancy (eV) |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 2 × 2 | 6 | A/B | 12.457795 | 6.228898 |
| 3 × 3 | 16 | A/A | 14.034173 | 7.017087 |
| 4 × 4 | 30 | A/B | 13.710196 | 6.855098 |
| 5 × 5 | 48 | A/B | 13.913360 | 6.956680 |
| 6 × 6 | 70 | A/A | 13.905304 | 6.952652 |
| 7 × 7 | 96 | A/B | 13.830592 | 6.915296 |
| 8 × 8 | 126 | A/B | 13.836803 | 6.918401 |
| 9 × 9 | 160 | A/A | 13.820776 | 6.910388 |
| 10 × 10 | 198 | A/B | 13.807627 | 6.903813 |

![Formation energy of the two-vacancy honeycomb arrays.](04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/formation_energy.png)

All nine relaxations reached maximum force below 0.005 eV/Å, and fresh MACE
evaluations verified their saved energies and forces. Perfect supercells at
every size agree with $2n^2\mu_\mathrm{C}$ to within $3\times10^{-12}$ eV.
Explicit 7 × 7 repeats checked equal vacancy distances and 120° angles.

The 7 × 7 through 10 × 10 energies span 13.8076–13.8368 eV for both vacancies.
Sizes 3, 6 and 9 use A/A parent sublattices, and the other sizes use A/B.
This scan varies vacancy concentration and parent-sublattice arrangement;
the small spread at its larger sizes does not establish the global-minimum
reconstruction or the dilute-vacancy limit.

See the [combined CSV](04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/formation_energies.csv),
[relaxation and extraction script](04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/relax.py), and
[plotting script](04_vacancy_formation_energy_2_10/plot_formation_energy.py).
The plotting script calls `plt.show()` by default.

## Reference setup

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| First local structure | Two-vacancy graphene monolayers, 4 × 4 and 5 × 5 |
| First observable | In-plane atomic displacement magnitude |
| Code, version and method | ASE 3.29.0; MACE 0.3.16; MACE-MPA-0 medium |
| Initial relaxation criterion | Maximum force below 0.005 eV/Å |
| Reference for displacement | Ideal surviving sites in the same fixed periodic cell |

## Strain protocol

Define the strain tensor, reference cell, directions and range. Record which cell
components are constrained and whether internal coordinates or transverse cell
components relax at each strain. Include the unstrained point as a baseline.

## Calculation record

For each run, record its identifier, structure source, strain, method/settings,
input and output paths, convergence status and extracted property with units.
The first relaxation records are in `02_vacancy_relaxation/4x4/metrics.json` and
`02_vacancy_relaxation/5x5/metrics.json`, with inputs, logs and trajectories beside them.

## Next step

Decide how to estimate the strain tensor from the discrete displacement field.
Before making quantitative physical claims, check the reference lattice constant,
vacancy reconstruction and cell-size effects against a suitable reference method.
